summary: Frauenfeld runs its main surface car parks itself (Marktplatz, Oberes and Unteres Mätteli, Altstadt streets) and says six of the 14 public car parks or garages in town are city-owned, while the large garages near the old town are mostly private and outside city price control. The main policy thread is a gradual shift of space towards other uses: the 2021 brochure counted a net loss of 42 centre spaces over ten years and warned of further cuts at the Mätteli sites, and voters turned down the city's participation in 50 public garage spaces in the cantonal building. A CHF 11.3 million inner-city street upgrade, approved in 2022, is now at public exhibition (August 2026), with some spaces on Freie-Strasse, Promenade and Rheinstrasse to be replaced via a swap with the canton and building from 2027 to 2030 subject to appeals. The Stadtrat approved a Smart Parking interim report on 18 August 2026: the camera-based occupancy measurement started in November 2023, was extended to 31 December 2027, and feeds the planned total revision of the Parkierungsreglement. Political friction continues, with an SVP inquiry in January 2026 about parking cuts and lost fee income, and a draft private-parking regulation that would raise the replacement levy from CHF 8,000 to CHF 10,000 per space. Current CHF tariffs, the fee regulation and EV charging details could not be confirmed from readable official pages.

items.text: Ahead of the 26 September 2021 vote, the Stadtrat said it wants a revised parking regulation that sets fees so they steer traffic, not only recover costs, and therefore wants car parks whose tariffs the city controls. It put the city's special 'Parkierung' fund, fed by replacement levies and parking fees, at just under CHF 6 million at end-2020, growing by about CHF 150,000 a year.
items.source_title: Abstimmungsbotschaft: 50 öffentliche Parkplätze im Ergänzungsbau Regierungsgebäude (Volksabstimmung 26. September 2021)

items.text: According to the Stadtrat in 2021, only two garages near the old town have public participation: the 63 public spaces in the Marktplatz building (open 24 hours) and Parkhaus Altstadt (open 07:00-21:00, city contribution CHF 2 million in 2013). Garages such as Schlosspark, Passage and Haus am Bahnhof are privately run, and the city has no influence on their hours or tariffs.
items.source_title: Abstimmungsbotschaft: 50 öffentliche Parkplätze im Ergänzungsbau Regierungsgebäude (Volksabstimmung 26. September 2021)

items.text: The Stadtrat stated in 2021 that counts put utilisation of Parkhaus Altstadt at about 30% and of the Marktplatz garage at about 65%. Opponents of the credit argued the Altstadt garage was mostly nearly empty and counted about 2,000 publicly accessible spaces in the inner city, about half underground.
items.source_title: Abstimmungsbotschaft: 50 öffentliche Parkplätze im Ergänzungsbau Regierungsgebäude (Volksabstimmung 26. September 2021)

items.text: The Gemeinderat approved 25 to 14 on 17 March 2021 a CHF 1.75 million credit (CHF 35,000 per space) to secure 50 public spaces in the new cantonal government building garage; opponents forced a referendum, scheduled for 26 September 2021. The Stadtrat expected the cantonal building to open around end-2024 or early 2025.
items.source_title: Abstimmungsbotschaft: 50 öffentliche Parkplätze im Ergänzungsbau Regierungsgebäude (Volksabstimmung 26. September 2021)

items.text: The 2021 brochure listed past losses: over ten years the city centre lost 42 public spaces net, and 160 spaces north of the station were removed with 143 created at Unteres Mätteli. It also said about 40 spaces at Unteres Mätteli were expected to go for a cultural pavilion, and that further reductions at Oberes Mätteli were open because of the planned 'Markt Thurgau' and barracks-site reuse.
items.source_title: Abstimmungsbotschaft: 50 öffentliche Parkplätze im Ergänzungsbau Regierungsgebäude (Volksabstimmung 26. September 2021)

items.text: The 15 May 2022 voting brochure put a CHF 11.3 million credit for upgrading inner-city streets to a vote, plus the question 'Altstadt autofrei?', defined as pedestrian zones with no car parking for visitors and residents. If the car-free option were rejected, a 20 km/h Begegnungszone with a reduced number of parking spaces on Freie-Strasse would apply. The brochure's opposing arguments also refer to the earlier rejection of the city's participation in the 50-space garage.
items.source_title: Abstimmungsbotschaft Rahmenkredit Aufwertung Strassenräume Innenstadt und Grundsatzfrage «Altstadt autofrei?» (15. Mai 2022)

items.text: SVP Gemeinderätin Christa Zahnd filed a Einfache Anfrage asking how many public parking spaces existed on 1 January 2020 and 31 July 2025, how many will remain on 31 December 2027, and what revenue loss the Stadtrat expects against 2019. She links possible space losses to the Verkehrskonzept Frauenfeld Ost, the inner-city street credit and the bicycle priority route; the Stadtrat's answer was due mid-February 2026 and was not found.
items.source_title: Anfrage an den Frauenfelder Stadtrat: Angst vor Parkplatzabbau und Umsatzverlust (Luzerner Zeitung)

items.text: The city's draft total revision of its private-parking regulation (version of 1 July 2025) proposes raising the replacement levy for a missing car space from CHF 8,000 to CHF 10,000, and sets lower space requirements than the VSS standard where practice shows it is too high. The Stadtrat released an earlier draft for consultation on 18 June 2024; it ran 28 June to 30 September 2024 and drew 12 submissions, and later approval steps were still blank.
items.source_title: Abstellplatzreglement Totalrevision: Erläuternder Bericht und Synopse (Version 1. Juli 2025)

items.text: In the August 2026 information on the inner-city street projects, the city says some spaces on Promenade, Freie-Strasse and Rheinstrasse must be removed but will be replaced, partly through a swap with the canton that opens more public spaces at the Obergericht and moves cantonal spaces into Parkgarage Altstadt. The plans were on public exhibition in August 2026 (until 2 September); building is planned for Zürcherstrasse 2027-28, Freie-Strasse, Rheinstrasse, Rathausplatz and Ringstrasse 2028-29, and Promenade from 2030, subject to appeals.
items.source_title: Strassenraum ist Lebensraum: Information zu den Auflage-Projekten Schlüsselgebiet Innenstadt

items.text: The Stadtrat approved on 18 August 2026 an interim report on Smart Parking. The pilot ran from 1 November 2023 to 30 November 2024, continuation to 31 December 2027 was approved in December 2024, and a final report with a recommendation to continue or stop is due in autumn 2027.
items.source_title: Mitteilungen aus dem Stadtrat vom 18. August 2026

items.text: The same notice says the occupancy data is meant to feed the planning of monitored car parks, communal master planning and the total revision of the Parkierungsreglement, and that use of the Regio Frauenfeld app is rising continuously. The city describes the system as an alternative to a classic sign-based Parkleitsystem.
items.source_title: Mitteilungen aus dem Stadtrat vom 18. August 2026

items.text: The city says Frauenfeld has 14 public car parks or garages, six of them city-owned; 24 cameras measure occupancy every 2 minutes at five car parks (Unteres Mätteli, Oberes Mätteli, Marktplatz, Altstadt Freie-Strasse/Bankplatz, Zürcherstrasse), with Parkhaus Altstadt added from September 2025 without cameras. Funding is about half Metropolitanraum Zürich and half the city's parking fund, with Parquery AG as technology partner; the page is undated and was read on 21 October 2026.

The Thurgau open-data portal lists the Frauenfeld occupancy dataset for five city-owned car parks (including Marktplatz as separate 2-hour and 10-hour areas), updated every 5 minutes, and warns the data are unvalidated measurements. The page was read on 21 October 2026 and showed 20 October 2026 as its issue and modification date.

Resident parking permits are issued for four zones (Ergaten, Kurzdorf, Mühletobel, Eisenwerk) as annual permits via the Parkingpay app, for CHF 30; regular overnight parking on public ground is charged separately. The page is undated and was read on 21 October 2026; no commuter permit was listed.

A city-hosted table of paid car parks (headed 'Stand: März 2018', file last modified July 2024, read on 21 October 2026) shows Mätteli and Unteres Mätteli chargeable Monday-Friday 08:00-19:00, free on Saturday, with a maximum stay of 8 days. It shows Marktplatz at 2 hours (Thundorferstrasse side) and 1 day (Marktstrasse side), and Bankplatz at 1 hour, charged until 17:00 on Saturday; it gives no CHF prices and may be out of date.

Thurplus lists three public charging stations in Frauenfeld, each with two 22 kW connectors running on local solar power. The page is undated and was read on 21 October 2026; the city also ended its two-year Sharemobil e-carsharing pilot on 24 February 2025 (Thurplus news of 7 February 2025, same site).

gaps: Browser-pane tab could not be opened (tabs_create failed), so pages were read as full text via curl plus a local HTML-to-text script, and PDFs via pypdf in isolated mode.

Parkingpay (parkingpay.ch) returns 403 behind a Cloudflare challenge: https://www.parkingpay.ch/de/frauenfeld. No current CHF hourly or daily tariffs for Marktplatz, Mätteli, Bankplatz or Parkhaus Marktplatz were found.

The legal text of the Parkierungsreglement and fee rules on https://frauenfeld.tlex.ch (JavaScript app) could not be read, so the fee regime in force and the draft Parkierungsreglement revision are not documented.
Night-parking flyer https://www.frauenfeld.ch/public/upload/assets/34321/Flyer%20Nachtparkieren.pdf is an image-only PDF with no extractable text, so night-parking fees are unknown.

Cantonal answer on the 2021 garage credit https://parlament.tg.ch/public/upload/assets/122287/05_Beantwortung_EA_Fehlende_Nachfrage_Tiefgaragenplaetze_FF.pdf returns 404. Luzerner Zeitung articles on the 2022 votes (e.g. ld.2383153) are paywalled and were not used.

No official page with vote counts was found for the 26 September 2021 vote on the 50 garage spaces or the 15 May 2022 vote on 'Altstadt autofrei?'; only the 2022 brochure's reference to the rejection of the garage credit and the 2026 city statement that voters approved the CHF 11.3 million credit in 2022.

The Stadtrat answer to the SVP inquiry of January 2026, the parking effects of the cantonal Verkehrskonzept Frauenfeld Ost, the current status of 'Markt Thurgau' / barracks site and Oberes Mätteli, any Parkhaus or P+R Bahnhof plans, commuter permits, and the Thurplus charger locations table were not found or not readable.
WebSearch budget ran out and frauenfeld.ch began returning HTTP 429, so further news (Thurgauer Zeitung, Frauenfelder Woche, SRF) and the press-release list could not be searched or opened.
